intro: These words come from German-language newspapers printed in the United States in the 1800s and early 1900s, held by the Library of Congress. They are printed in Fraktur, a blackletter type. The long ſ looks like an f without the crossbar, and r, x, k, t, B and V can look alike. The long ſ and the round s count as the same letter, so they are never highlighted.
name: German
title: German newspapers
